short: A unique code for one exact sellable variant.
seoTitle: SKU — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: An SKU, or stock keeping unit, is a unique code for one exact sellable variant — a specific product in a specific size, colour and pack.
definition: An SKU, or stock keeping unit, is a unique code for one exact sellable variant — a specific product in a specific size, colour and pack. Two variants of the same product are two SKUs.
bodyHtml:
Why SKU matters

SKUs are the unit everything else counts in. Stock levels, reorder points, margin analysis and sales reporting all depend on being able to tell a 500 ml bottle from a 1 litre one.

How SKU works in practice

Build codes that a human can read at a glance — brand, category, size — and never reuse a retired code for a new product. Reuse silently merges two products' sales history into one misleading line.

Worked example

AMU-MLK-500 and AMU-MLK-1000 are separate SKUs for the same brand of milk in two pack sizes.

faq.question: Is an SKU the same as a barcode?
faq.answer: No. A barcode is a scannable number, often assigned by the manufacturer; an SKU is your own internal identifier.

faq.question: How many SKUs should a small shop have?
faq.answer: As many as it genuinely sells. Every extra SKU is stock, shelf space and counting time, which is what ABC analysis is for.
